sources.t: ADR schemes' performance
sources.f: Updated 23 July 2026; Ofcom publishes quarterly KPI results for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
sources.g: ADR performance measures complaint handling and does not prove network reach or current orderability at a premises.

sources.t: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business
sources.f: Published 13 February 2026; Ofcom explains contract transfer, switching and service continuity scenarios when a provider ceases trading.
sources.g: Consumer continuity guidance presupposes a service relationship and is not exact parcel availability evidence.

sources.t: Making a complaint and using alternative dispute resolution schemes
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; Ofcom explains formal complaints and access to approved ADR schemes after unresolved disputes.
sources.g: Complaint rights and provider membership do not establish serviceability at an address.

sources.t: Contracts
sources.f: Updated 26 June 2026; Ofcom summarises contract summaries, price changes, termination and service-level considerations.
sources.g: Contract rules apply after product selection and do not prove that a network reaches a parcel.

sources.t: Broadband and landline faults and problems
sources.f: Updated 8 April 2026; Ofcom provides fault identification, repair, compensation and complaint guidance.
sources.g: Fault guidance describes existing customer services and cannot establish initial address orderability.

sources.t: Pricing and consumer engagement
sources.f: Updated 26 February 2026; the report covers residential communications prices, switching, affordability and debt.
sources.g: National market research and tariff analysis are not exact premises connectivity evidence.

sources.t: Pricing and consumer engagement 2025 interactive report
sources.f: Published 26 February 2026; the interactive report presents trends in fixed broadband, voice, mobile and pay-TV pricing and engagement.
sources.g: Interactive market statistics do not prove a provider can serve a specific parcel.

sources.t: Unable to pay a bill?
sources.f: Updated 8 April 2026; Ofcom explains payment difficulty, disputed charges, restriction and ADR options.
sources.g: Billing support evidence is unrelated to physical network availability at an address.

sources.t: Notifying a phone or broadband provider of a customer's death
sources.f: Updated 8 April 2026; Ofcom explains fair account closure, transfer and complaint handling after bereavement.
sources.g: Account administration guidance does not establish coverage or current retail orderability.

sources.t: Using your mobile abroad
sources.f: Updated 6 July 2026; Ofcom explains roaming charges, alerts, limits and ways to control overseas costs.
sources.g: Roaming protections and tariffs are not fixed-broadband or exact parcel evidence.

sources.t: Communications Affordability Tracker
sources.f: Updated 14 May 2026; Ofcom reports research on affordability of broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV services.
sources.g: Survey findings and affordability indicators do not establish address-level coverage.

sources.t: Mobile phone service faults and problems
sources.f: Updated 8 April 2026; Ofcom provides guidance on diagnosing and reporting mobile faults and checking expected coverage.
sources.g: Fault diagnosis and predicted coverage do not guarantee service at a specific premises.

sources.t: BT's landline-only customers
sources.f: Updated 16 March 2026; Ofcom records protections and pricing context for BT landline-only customers.
sources.g: Customer-group regulation does not prove current infrastructure availability for a parcel.

sources.t: Upgrading landlines to digital technology
sources.f: Updated 16 September 2024; Ofcom explains migration from PSTN to VoIP and power-cut considerations.
sources.g: Technology migration guidance does not establish retail broadband orderability at an address.

sources.t: Complain about mobile, phone or internet services
sources.f: Official complaint hub routes billing, contract, fault, switching and service complaints.
sources.g: Complaint routing is consumer-process evidence, not parcel connectivity evidence.

sources.t: Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme information
sources.f: Updated 16 March 2026; BDUK explains voucher eligibility, availability and supplier-led project operation.
sources.g: Voucher eligibility and funding do not prove that a completed, orderable connection exists at a premises.

sources.t: Project Gigabit framework agreement – Openreach
sources.f: Updated 2 March 2026; BDUK describes the cross-regional Openreach framework for hard-to-reach premises.
sources.g: Framework and call-off scope are planned delivery evidence, not current exact-address service confirmation.

sources.t: User guide and technical note for premises in BDUK plans
sources.f: The technical guide explains UPRN-level inputs, OMR derivation, management information and interpretation limits.
sources.g: BDUK's current view and planned-delivery records require fresh provider and orderability validation before parcel promotion.

sources.t: Open Market Review determinations and BDUK plans
sources.f: Published 1 July 2025; the collection provides OMR outcomes and BDUK views of current, planned and intervention connectivity.
sources.g: The collection combines current and future classifications and is not a live retail order check.

sources.t: A Councillor's Guide to Project Gigabit
sources.f: Updated 4 February 2025; the guide explains Project Gigabit delivery, local impacts and council participation.
sources.g: Programme guidance and local deployment context do not establish current service at an individual premises.
